thread:
Helen: FYI quickstart on Win10 flakily outputs garbled JSON after system sleep/resume while streaming. Repro steps in a sec.
Marco: steps?
Helen: 1) chrome on win10, 2) start streaming chat from quickstart, 3) put machine to sleep for ~8s, 4) resume. Often see "Unexpected token" parse errors and UI shows partial HTML.
Devon: which SDK/version?
Helen: browser-sdk 0.11.1 from quickstart bundle. Node sample-app seemed fine.
Marco: can you paste raw stream capture?
Helen: snippet from network inspector (trimmed):
```data: {"id":"s1","chunk":"{\"text\":\"ok\"}"}

data: {"id":"s1","chunk":"{\"text\":\"resume\"}"}
```
But after sleep sometimes we get merged buffers like `...}

data: {` becoming `...}
data: {` (no CRLF pair) and our simple line-splitter produces `}
data:` as content which breaks JSON boundary detection.
Devon: hmm Windows TCP stack + Chrome suspend maybe collapsing the two CRLFs into a single LF on resume? That would break an SSE parser expecting double-newline to end event.
Marco: short-term workaround for demo: server can include an explicit sentinel line `data: [CHUNK_END]

` between logical frames. Also mention in onboarding notes to avoid sleeping the laptop during demo.
Helen: added a note to quickstart README.
Devon: SDK fix idea: make browser SSE parser treat any lone LF followed by `data:` as if a CRLFCRLF existed. Basically normalize `\n\ndata:` and `\ndata:` edgecases by re-checking previous byte; and keep a tiny buffer (40ms) to allow remainder to arrive before failing parse.
Marco: also add diagnostics flag to emit raw byte boundary logs so QA can paste the binary chunk boundaries when filing bugs.
qa-bot: Created ticket QA/STREAM-411: "quickstart: garbled SSE on Windows sleep/resume"
ci-bot: Created issue devex/sdk-js#3021: "browser SSE: normalize single-LF resume boundaries and add reassembly window"
Helen: we should also add an e2e that runs headless Chrome, simulates sleep/resume (suspend+resume) with a throttled network to catch regressions.
Devon: agreed; I'll prototype a unit test that fakes mid-buffer LF merges and assert parser tolerates it.
Marco: thanks all, this should reduce weird onboarding failures. :thumbsup:
